about: Every shared Street Kit asset, planned and painted. The docs site (https://danbhala.github.io/street-kit/) is built from this file. When an asset is painted: set status to 'shipped', fill spritecook and outputs, and set since to the release it ships in.

assets.name: Semi-detached house front

uses.tip-the-can: Backdrop band, street map, title screen
uses.kerby: Mid parallax layer and "pick your house"

spritecook.prompt: The front of one red-brick 1930s British semi-detached house seen straight-on from the street, flat front elevation, side-on, not angled: hipped grey slate roof with a chimney, white UPVC bay window with net curtains downstairs, a window upstairs with pebble-dash panel, white UPVC porch and front door, a satellite dish on the wall. Only this one house, no ground, no garden, no people.

The front of one 1930s British semi-detached house, the same house as the reference, but the whole front in cream pebble-dash render: white UPVC bay window with net curtains, hipped grey slate roof, chimney, white UPVC porch and front door. Seen straight-on from the street, flat front elevation, not angled. Only this, no ground, no pavement, no people, transparent background.

assets.notes: Red brick painted in Kerby's test batch (kerby-game art/street/house_semi.png), shipped in 0.2.0; pebble-dash painted with it as the reference, shipped in 0.3.0. Use the red-brick one as a second style reference for every elevation.

uses.tip-the-can: Could sit in the sky band or title screen, graded to dusk

spritecook.prompt: A long row of distant British suburban rooftops seen from far away: pitched roofs, chimney stacks with pots, TV aerials, a satellite dish and a few rounded tree crowns, painted as one flat soft silhouette band in muted dusky mauve with only very faint lighter edges where the low sun catches the roof ridges, no windows, no detail, no outlines. Front elevation, a straight horizontal strip filling the width, ends cut square, flat bottom edge. No ground, no sky, no cast shadow.

assets.notes: Painted in Kerby's batches as one soft muted-mauve band, further away than the detailed roofline strip.

assets.name: Granite kerb section

uses.kerby: The kerb you throw at: the gameplay strip

spritecook.prompt: A straight section of British granite kerb stones seen side-on from a slightly elevated camera about 20 degrees down: a thin strip of paving slabs on top, the pale kerb stones with a crisp bright sunlit highlight running along the kerb's rounded top front edge, the kerb's vertical front face in soft shade, and a narrow strip of dark tarmac gutter at the bottom. Runs straight across the whole frame, horizontal, no objects, no people.

assets.notes: Seen from about 20 degrees down, so it suits Kerby's camera; Tip the Can has no use for it. The highlight sits just under the top edge, so Kerby draws its own hit-zone line.
